posts.author: p1ece0FShimata
posts.body: Hi, I don't know if this question has been asked before (I haven't seen a video on this issue), but how do you make normal animations in cutscenes? Like for exemple, a person is sitting at a desk typing, you can talk to them. Then after an event, they stand up and leave, and after that, the desk and chair become tilesets. I just don't understand how to do that. Do I need to work with animations editor in RPG Maker, or create an animation like the player's? Or maybe set the chair and desk as tiles and add an animation on top using an event? I really just don't understand the best way to approach this.

posts.author: KaijuuKimi
posts.body: You dont need the build in animation editor. Simple animation can be done just by using the actor stepping animation and changing the actor direction in an event. For more complex stuff, you may require advance eventing knowledge and using plugins but it is possible.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
p1ece0FShimata said:
I know that you need to add !$ at the beginning of the filename if the sprite is non-standard size, but it still doesn't change the sprite capture.
Click to expand...
That is because your knowledge is wrong.
! is a flag for object sprites, which means the regular shift of a few pixels up that applies to people sprites to make them seem to walk inside the grid instead of on its borders is disabled.
$ is a flag for a single sprite as opposed to a spritesheet of 8 sprites.
the RPG-Makers can use any sprite size without any flag as long as you follow the sprite/spritesheet specifications. I once wrote a tutorial that explains this in more detail:
How to create your own templates (any sprite or battler sheet) | RPG Maker Forums

posts.author: KaijuuKimi
posts.body: Large monster use $ because they are characters and their sprites are actually just stepping animation in different direction. Using $ for your character makes finding them easier because you can name them instead of 8 character in 1 large sprite sheet. Your sprite size can be any size as long as it follow the format 4x3/8x2 and under 1024 pixel square

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
p1ece0FShimata said:
It cut the sprite, and I can't seem to stop it from doing that.
Click to expand...
The frame you use to select is what I called a 'Cell' in the tutorial I linked above.
That is the basic unit of a sprite, and it is determined by the total size of the spritesheet.
or more precise, it is one third the width and one fourth the height of the total sprite.
if the frame is too small, that means you need to increase the size of the total sprite - WITHOUT increasing the size og the picture inside the frame/sprite.
And that is the reason why I told in the tutorial to determine the size of the cell first before calculating what size you need for the sprite.
